plan.title: Confounded lung treated vs control DE + enrichment
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 6 treated vs 6 control lung samples with raw salmon counts, but batch B1 holds every control and batch B2 holds every treated sample — the batch is perfectly confounded with condition (design knowledge service rule R-0005, flag: confounded_label_or_stop). A model matrix cannot separate 'treatment effect' from 'batch effect' here, and any batch-correction method (ComBat-seq, removeBatchEffect, SVA) would remove the condition signal along with the batch, or worse, fabricate a corrected effect that is not identifiable from this design. The only defensible path is: (1) run QC that explicitly visualizes the condition/batch overlap so the confound is documented rather than hidden, (2) fit DESeq2 with ~condition only (no batch term — it would make the design matrix rank-deficient anyway), (3) run the standard DESeq2 Wald/apeglm/BH pipeline, and (4) label every downstream result, every plot, and the enrichment output as confounded — the differences found could reflect treatment, batch (library prep, sequencing run, handling), or both, and this analysis cannot distinguish them. Enrichment proceeds as a discrete-list GO over-representation test (clusterProfiler enrichGO + rrvgo term reduction) using the tested-gene universe, since the knowledge check rejected a ranked fgsea/Hallmark run as outside the permitted method set for this flagged design; ORA against Hallmark/Reactome/MSigDB-canonical gene sets (all staged locally) follows as a secondary, equally-caveated check. No result from this analysis should be interpreted as a validated treatment effect without an independent, deconfounded cohort.
